summary: Mid-stream client disconnect cancels generation; query completes server-side instead
description:
When a user navigates away mid-stream, controller.enqueue() throws and the for-await loop in src/app/api/query/route.ts breaks (line ~250). Breaking the async iterator calls .return() on the OpenRouter SDK stream, which aborts the upstream fetch and CANCELS generation at the provider. Result: no final usage chunk arrives, so input/output tokens + cost_usd persist as NULL (rendered as 0/$0.00 in the admin view) and only the partial response text is saved.

Users coming from ChatGPT/Claude expect an answer to finish server-side and be waiting in the thread when they return. Fix: on client disconnect, stop pushing bytes to the dead socket but KEEP draining the upstream stream to completion, so the full response + real usage get persisted and billed normally. Deployment is a long-lived Node server (Hetzner VPS via next start), so the route handler keeps executing after disconnect.

Decision (user-confirmed): scope = complete + save server-side only (no live-resume reconnection); abandoned queries now cost full generation, bounded by existing rate-limit + budget reservation.
